title: Derived base change for a relatively flat module
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism of schemes,
and let $\mathcal G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module flat
over $S$. For every $g:T\to S$, derived pullback gives an isomorphism

$$
Lg^*Rf_*\mathcal G\;\cong\;Rf_{T,*}\mathcal G_T.
$$

proof.text: Write $p:X_T\to X$ and $f_T:X_T\to T$ for the projections and $\theta:Lg^*Rf_*\mathcal G\to Rf_{T,*}\mathcal G_T$ for the base change map of [lem-pc-base-change-map-cech] (adjoint to $Rf_*\mathcal G\to Rf_*Rp_*p^*\mathcal G=Rg_*Rf_{T,*}\mathcal G_T$). Being an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is checked on the cohomology sheaves, hence on affine opens $W\subseteq g^{-1}(V)$, $V\subseteq S$ affine; restriction to opens is exact and commutes with $Rf_*$ and $Lg^*$, so $\theta$ restricts to the base change map for $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ and $W\to V$. Thus take $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$, and choose a finite affine open cover $X=\bigcup_i U_i$ (quasi-compactness). Since $X\to S$ is separated, every finite intersection $U_J=\operatorname{Spec}(C_J)$ is affine. The node [lem-pc-cech-resolution] gives the bounded Cech complex $K^\bullet$, $K^p=\prod_{|J|=p+1}\Gamma(U_J,\mathcal G)$, whose associated sheaf complex $\widetilde{K^\bullet}$ computes $Rf_*\mathcal G$.

source.place: Proof, local affine reduction and Cech resolution

proof.text: For every intersection $U_J=\operatorname{Spec}(C_J)$, quasi-coherence identifies $N_J=\Gamma(U_J,\mathcal G)$ with the module defining $\mathcal G|_{U_J}$. Relative flatness of $\mathcal G$ over $S$ says that each $N_J$ is flat over $A$. A finite product of flat $A$-modules is flat (apply the injectivity criterion for flatness coordinatewise), so every term of the finite Cech complex $K^\bullet$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: Proof, flatness of the Cech terms

proof.text: Each $\widetilde{K^p}$ is a flat $\mathcal O_S$-module (its stalks are localizations of the flat $A$-module $K^p$), and $\widetilde{K^\bullet}$ is bounded, so [lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback] shows that the canonical map $Lg^*\widetilde{K^\bullet}\to g^*\widetilde{K^\bullet}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_T)$; and $g^*\widetilde{K^\bullet}=(K^\bullet\otimes_AB)^\sim$ termwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] applied to $g$ with $V=S$, $U=T$.

source.place: Proof, derived pullback of the flat Cech complex

proof.text: The pullbacks $U_J\times_ST=p^{-1}(U_J)=\operatorname{Spec}(C_J\otimes_AB)$ are affine and form a finite affine cover of $X_T$ with intersections $U_J\times_ST$; let $K_T^\bullet$ be its Cech complex for $\mathcal G_T=p^*\mathcal G$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] to $p$ with $V=U_J$, $U=p^{-1}(U_J)$ shows that the map $c_J:N_J\otimes_{C_J}(C_J\otimes_AB)=N_J\otimes_AB\to\Gamma(U_J\times_ST,\mathcal G_T)$, $s\otimes b\mapsto b\cdot(p^*s)|_{U_J\times_ST}$, is an isomorphism for every $J$. These are the components of the cochain map $\gamma:K^\bullet\otimes_AB\to K_T^\bullet$ of [lem-pc-base-change-map-cech], so $\gamma$ is an isomorphism of complexes.

source.place: Proof, pullback cover and tensor identification of sections

proof.text: By [lem-pc-base-change-map-cech], $\theta$ is the composite $Lg^*\widetilde{K^\bullet}\to g^*\widetilde{K^\bullet}=(K^\bullet\otimes_AB)^\sim\xrightarrow{\tilde\gamma}\widetilde{K_T^\bullet}$, read through the identifications $Rf_*\mathcal G\cong\widetilde{K^\bullet}$ and $Rf_{T,*}\mathcal G_T\cong\widetilde{K_T^\bullet}$ of [lem-pc-cech-resolution] (the latter for the pullback cover, $X_T\to T$ being separated and quasi-compact). The first arrow is an isomorphism by Step 3 and $\tilde\gamma$ by Step 4, so $\theta$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, comparison with the pullback Cech resolution
